evidence: DeformX models DLOs as Cosserat rods; the framework is a direct application of Cosserat rod theory.
Rod engine uses a discrete Cosserat formulation in the Bergou-Audoly DER family (vertices + per-edge SO(3) frames).
Object class targeted by the framework.
Sim-to-real transfer of policies trained in DeformX is the paper's central empirical claim.
Paper proposes the multi-rate Cosserat-rod + Isaac Sim co-simulation pattern; this is the paper's primary architectural contribution.
Rope-swinging hit-target task on UR5e: DeformX vs. Isaac linked-capsule baseline reduces real-world tip-to-goal error from 15.1/25.9/30.4 cm to 6.6/7.3/5.8 cm across three targets, n=10 each.

Rope is one of four deformable object classes benchmarked; the JAX simulator's rope manipulation tasks (Push-Rope, Whip-Rope) and sim-to-real real-robot evaluation (Push-Rope on Kinova Gen3) directly target DLOs.

DaX models cloth dynamics with a mass-spring system (mesh-based) — paper Section 3.1 / appendix sec:object_model. Rationale: cloth undergoes only limited deformation, so the simpler mass-spring model is preferred over MPM.
Sim-to-real claim: CEM-MPC + DaX deployed on a Kinova Gen3 for Push-Rope produces real-robot trajectories that closely track DaX-predicted next states (paper Section 4.4 + appendix sim2real).
Imitation Learning is one of the three benchmarked algorithm paradigms; baselines include Transporter (non-differentiable) and ILD (differentiable physics).
CEM-MPC and Diff-CEM-MPC use the simulator as predictive model and plan via cross-entropy elite resampling; this is the model-based-RL/MPC family.
Comparison with FEM-based DOM simulators (DiffSim) is part of Table 1 simulator_comparison; FEM is the alternative continuum baseline.
Transporter networks (one of two IL baselines benchmarked) is a behavioral-cloning style imitation learner over pick-and-place affordances.

DaXBench is the canonical instantiation of the multi-object differentiable DOM benchmark pattern: JAX-batched MLS-MPM (rope/liquid) + mass-spring (cloth) + 9 tasks + 8 algorithms across planning/IL/RL.
DaXBench Table RL_results (Whip-Rope): APG 0.83 ± 0.01, SHAC 0.66 ± 0.03, PPO 0.25 ± 0.10 over 20 seeds. APG dominates by 3.3x over PPO and 1.26x over SHAC.

DaXBench Whip-Rope: APG 0.83 / SHAC 0.66 vs CEM-MPC 0.34 / Diff-MPC 0.37 / Diff-CEM-MPC 0.33. JAX simulator achieves 128 batched rollouts of 80 timesteps (forward + backward) in ~3 s on 4 x 2080-Ti GPUs (paper Section sec:jax).
